goal: Investigate CVE-2024-3400 using live CVE, CISA KEV and EPSS evidence. If a source fails, revise your approach. Produce a cited report and explain missing asset context.

plan.objective: Gather and synthesize evidence for CVE-2024-3400 from the CVE Services record, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, and EPSS score, then assess applicability given missing asset context.

CISA KEV and EPSS APIs are reachable and will return data for the CVE if it is listed.

summary.text: CVE-2024-3400 is a critical command‑injection flaw in Palo Alto Networks PAN‑OS GlobalProtect that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges on affected firewalls. The CVE record was only retrieved from an official mirror after a primary‑source timeout.

findings.rationale: The vulnerability carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 10.0 (critical) and appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog with a known ransomware‑campaign use. EPSS assigns a score of 0.99999, indicating a high estimated 30‑day exploitation likelihood.
recommended_actions: Apply mitigations per Palo Alto Networks vendor instructions as they become available.
Enable Threat Prevention IDs provided by the vendor for vulnerable devices until a patch is released.
Monitor vendor bulletins for patch release schedules affecting PAN‑OS versions 10.2.0‑10.2.9‑h1, 11.0.0‑11.0.4‑h1, and 11.1.0‑11.1.2‑h3.
uncertainties: The CVE record was obtained from an official mirror after a primary‑source timeout, so the completeness of the record cannot be fully verified.
Applicability to specific assets cannot be confirmed without knowing the exact PAN‑OS version and GlobalProtect configuration in use.
Current patch status is not reflected in the retrieved evidence; verification with the vendor is required.

limitations: E001 indicates a primary‑source timeout; the CVE data used comes from an official mirror and may be incomplete.
The investigation reflects the state of the KEV catalog and EPSS score at the time of retrieval; later updates are not captured.

descriptions:
A command injection as a result of arbitrary file creation vulnerability in the GlobalProtect feature of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software for specific PAN-OS versions and distinct feature configurations may enable an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.

Cloud NGFW, Panorama appliances, and Prisma Access are not impacted by this vulnerability.

entry.vulnerabilityName: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Command Injection Vulnerability
entry.shortDescription: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect feature contains a command injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands with root privileges on the firewall.
entry.requiredAction: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions as they become available. Otherwise, users with vulnerable versions of affected devices should enable Threat Prevention IDs available from the vendor. See the vendor bulletin for more details and a patch release schedule.
